clients.ficha.invoicesLockedBody: Invoices are not linked to the client yet: only its name is stored, as text. We can't show a balance here without making it up.
clients.ficha.appearsInBody: The client picker when creating a jobsite, the “Client” filter of the jobsite list and the printed recipient of the invoice.

clients.ficha.obras.error.title: We couldn't fetch its jobsites.
clients.ficha.facturas.title: Invoices are not linked to the client yet. They'll show here once they are.
tour.welcome.title: Welcome to your panel!
tour.welcome.body: Let us show you where everything lives — under a minute, no jargon, just what you need to get going today.
tour.welcome.quick1: Create your first jobsite in Projects.
tour.welcome.quick3: Hand them their QR badge so they can clock in from their phone.
tour.step.dashboard.title: Your day at a glance
tour.step.dashboard.body: Everything in one view: who worked today, hours logged and the latest activity.
tour.step.users.title: Your crew
tour.step.users.body: Add your workers here and generate their QR badge. That's what they use to clock in and out from their phone.
tour.step.time-approvals.title: Approve hours
tour.step.time-approvals.body: The hours your crew clocks land here for you to review and approve before they count toward pay.
tour.step.projects.title: Your jobsites
tour.step.projects.body: Every project lives here. Hours, expenses and invoices always tie back to a project.
tour.step.invoices.title: The money
tour.step.invoices.body: Everything about money lives in this group: invoices, budgets, expenses, what you're owed and what you owe.
tour.step.audit.title: Change history
tour.step.audit.body: Every important action is recorded: who did what, and when. Your backup whenever questions come up.
tour.step.billing.title: Your subscription
tour.step.billing.body: Manage your plan and service payments here.
tour.step.help.title: Want to see this again?
tour.step.help.body: This button replays the tour anytime. That's it — go build!

tour.step.money.title: Money first
tour.step.money.body: What you're owed (already late), what you owe this week, and expenses waiting on you. Orange means it needs your attention.
tour.step.today.title: On site today
tour.step.today.body: Who clocked in, on which jobsite, and the hours waiting for your approval. If an active jobsite wakes up with no clock-ins, we flag it here.
tour.step.budget.title: Budget, watched
tour.step.budget.body: Every jobsite's consumption against its contract. Anything past 90% turns orange before it becomes a problem.
tour.step.pulse.title: Jobsite pulse
tour.step.pulse.body: Client calling? Pick the jobsite and in five seconds you have the latest site log, open items, the money and who worked today.
tour.step.favorites.title: Your favorites
tour.step.favorites.body: Hover any menu section and tap the star: it pins to the top under Favorites, one click away.
sec.hours.step.kpis.title: This screen never talks about money
sec.hours.step.kpis.body: Time only. "Pending hours" are entries you have not approved yet in the Approvals inbox, which is why they do not count as approved here.
sec.hours.step.filters.title: Project means where they clocked in
sec.hours.step.filters.body: The filter uses the project the worker punched into that day, not the one on their profile. And "attendance" isolates who was absent or late.
sec.hours.step.list.title: The row of little squares is the month
sec.hours.step.list.body: Each square is a day: black present, orange late, hollow absent. It comes from comparing the punched-in time against the project's schedule.
sec.labor-cost.step.kpis.title: This is projected cost, not paid
sec.labor-cost.step.kpis.body: Approved hours for the period times each user's hourly rate from their profile. The third number is workers with no rate — that is why they add nothing to the total.
sec.labor-cost.step.filters.title: Changing the range recalculates everything
sec.labor-cost.step.filters.body: Week to month does not filter the list: it recomputes the whole cost, because only approved hours dated inside the range count.
sec.labor-cost.step.list.title: Workers with no rate are grouped on top
sec.labor-cost.step.list.body: With an orange border. Until you set their hourly rate in Users, their hours are invisible to cost.
sec.labor-payroll.step.kpis.title: "To pay" is real money outstanding
sec.labor-payroll.step.kpis.body: Approved hours not yet marked as paid, times the worker's rate. The number in brackets warns how many people are blocked for having no rate.
sec.labor-payroll.step.filters.title: Paid is not the same as approved
sec.labor-payroll.step.filters.body: This dropdown filters by whether you already confirmed payment for the period, not by the approval status of the hours.
sec.labor-payroll.step.list.title: This is where money actually moves
sec.labor-payroll.step.list.body: Click a "to pay" row to confirm the payment: that amount is deducted from the project's budget. Already-paid rows are dimmed with their date.
sec.clients.step.add-client.title: The client you create here is used twice
sec.clients.step.add-client.body: It is the one you pick when creating a project, and the one printed as the recipient on the invoice.
sec.clients.step.search.title: It searches the server
sec.clients.step.search.body: By name, contact, phone or email across all your clients — not just the page you are looking at.
sec.clients-ficha.step.bar.title: Everything about the client, up top
sec.clients-ficha.step.bar.body: Its status, its tax ID and how long it has worked with you. These buttons edit or deactivate it.
sec.clients-ficha.step.tabs.title: Summary, jobsites and invoices
sec.clients-ficha.step.tabs.body: Summary is who to call and how they get invoiced; Jobsites, everything you have built for them. Invoices opens once they are linked to the client.
sec.clients-ficha.step.shortcuts.title: The two reasons to open a client
sec.clients-ficha.step.shortcuts.body: Copy its billing details for a document, or create a jobsite with it already picked.
sec.subcontractors.step.tabs.title: Two flows that meet
sec.subcontractors.step.tabs.body: "Jobs" is what you assign them. "Invoices" is what they bill you for it. And this first tab says where you stand with each of them.
sec.subcontractors.step.kpis.title: What you owe, added up
sec.subcontractors.step.kpis.body: The three figures are for the whole total, not the page. The balance is what they invoiced and you approved, minus what you've already paid.
sec.subcontractors.step.filters.title: Who owes you work and who owes money
sec.subcontractors.step.filters.body: Cross "with open jobs" and "with a balance due" to see at a glance who has something outstanding with you.
Click someone and you land on Jobs with their filter applied. Nobody is created here: that happens in Users.
sec.subcontractors-jobs.step.job-kpis.bo: Jobs the subcontractor has finished and left for your sign-off. Click the figure to see only those.
sec.subcontractors-jobs.step.job-filters: Filter by who and by jobsite
Search by title or by name, and cross subcontractor, jobsite and status. The search looks at every page, not just this one.
The two numbers at the end are their photos and their notes: at zero, they haven't uploaded anything yet.
sec.subcontractors-ficha.step.job-action: The two decisions of the day are on the bar. If you need to move the job to another status, use "Change status".
sec.subcontractors-ficha.step.money.titl: What you owe on this one
sec.subcontractors-ficha.step.money.body: What you agreed, what they invoiced, what you've paid and what's left. The balance comes from their approved invoices, not from memory.
sec.subcontractors-ficha.step.tabs.title: Their proof and your record
sec.subcontractors-ficha.step.tabs.body: "Evidence" holds their photos, videos and documents. "History" holds everything that has happened to the job and who did it.
sec.schedules.step.header.title: The day comes first
sec.schedules.step.header.body: Read this screen top to bottom like the morning report: the date, how many tasks are open and how many are past due. The numbers only count open work.
sec.schedules.step.views.title: Two views, one set of tasks
sec.schedules.step.views.body: List answers what's due now. Week answers who is overloaded and what overlaps. Same tasks from the other side; anything you do in one shows up in the other.
sec.schedules.step.filters.title: All your projects at once
sec.schedules.step.filters.body: You no longer pick a project to start: you land on all of them. The chips filter without reloading and carry each project's open count; person and step combine with them.
sec.schedules.step.groups.title: By urgency, not by step
sec.schedules.step.groups.body: Overdue, Due today, This week, No dates and Finished this week. In every row the button on the right is named after the next step: that's how work moves, and there's no going back once it's Completed.
sec.schedules.step.shortcuts.title: Without leaving the keyboard
sec.schedules.step.shortcuts.body: J and K move down and up, → advances the step and Enter opens the task. Completing and deleting always ask first. This bar keeps the shortcuts in sight.
sec.schedules-semana.step.rows.title: Every row is a person
sec.schedules-semana.step.rows.body: Rows are people and columns are days, so overload and overlaps show at a glance. Switch to Projects when what you want to compare is the sites themselves.
sec.schedules-semana.step.nav.title: What runs past the week
sec.schedules-semana.step.nav.body: A bar with an edge mark and a date keeps going beyond this week. Move between weeks with the arrows: it's the same task, you're just seeing another stretch of it.
sec.schedules-semana.step.undated.title: The no-dates drawer
sec.schedules-semana.step.undated.body: Tasks without dates don't fit in any week, so they live down here. Give them dates from the drawer and they drop into the calendar without opening anything.
sec.tool-inventory.step.header.title: Two inventories, two questions
sec.tool-inventory.step.header.body: A drill is lent and comes back: what matters is where it is and who answers for it. A screw gets used up: what matters is how much is left. Switch tabs and the question changes.
sec.tool-inventory.step.counts.title: The six numbers add up
sec.tool-inventory.step.counts.body: The total is the exact sum of the six states, and each cell filters the table. Watch "Awaiting acceptance": those already left the warehouse and nobody has signed for them.
sec.tool-inventory.step.filters.title: Search by code, filter by worker
sec.tool-inventory.step.filters.body: Search covers code and name, across the whole inventory, not just this page. The worker filter is for the day someone leaves: it tells you what they have and what's still out.
sec.tool-inventory.step.table.title: This is where you register and fix
sec.tool-inventory.step.table.body: Click a row and its record opens with the full history. Assigning, returning and dispatching happen in the warehouse, and a tool that's out doesn't change status until it comes back.
sec.tool-report.step.state.title: The six states add up
sec.tool-report.step.state.body: The total is the exact sum of the six states and the percentage column adds to 100. The sixth — awaiting acceptance: out of the warehouse and unsigned — wasn't included before, which is why the breakdown never closed.
sec.tool-report.step.missing.title: What hasn't come back
sec.tool-report.step.missing.body: The tools that have been out too long, or that left with nobody signing for them. This is the list to chase this week, with name and project. Damaged and lost ones aren't here: their status already says where they ended up.
sec.tool-report.step.filters.title: Filtering recalculates, it doesn't just hide
sec.tool-report.step.filters.body: When you filter, the whole report is requested again: figures, percentages and tables cover only what's filtered, and the scope is stated at the top. Supplies have their own categories, so they're included in full and the screen says so.
sec.tool-report.step.export.title: The paper is the product
sec.tool-report.step.export.body: The PDF is to sign and attach; the Excel, to keep working. Both are being rebuilt on the server so they come out with your filters on, in your language and with your company's logo; until then the button is off.
sec.invoices.step.summary.title: Three counts you do not add up yourself
sec.invoices.step.summary.body: Issued this month, receivable, and awaiting approval. The server counts them over all your documents, never over this page. The third one is a button: it takes you to the change orders the list hides.
sec.invoices.step.filters.title: Filter by jobsite, type, status and dates
sec.invoices.step.filters.body: All four filter on the server, so the result covers your whole account and not the loaded page. Note: with no status filter, the server does not return change orders awaiting approval.
sec.invoices.step.list.title: Everything you have issued
sec.invoices.step.list.body: Invoices and change orders with their status and what is left to collect. Each row's menu downloads its PDF again. Recording a payment does not happen here: that is Accounts Receivable.
sec.invoices.step.new.title: Issue a document
sec.invoices.step.new.body: Opens the window with the preview beside it. An invoice bills what was agreed; a change order asks for money outside the contract and starts out awaiting approval.
sec.invoices-emitir.title: Issue document — the window
sec.invoices-emitir.body: The form on the left, the document drawing itself on the right. On issue it is saved, the PDF downloads with its number, and the row appears in the list.
sec.invoices-emitir.b1: Pick the jobsite and we tell you what is left to bill against its contract, before you type anything.
sec.invoices-emitir.b2: Only billable jobsites are offered: neither closed, nor missing a client or cost code.
sec.invoices-emitir.step.type.title: An invoice and a change order are not the same
sec.invoices-emitir.step.type.body: An invoice bills what was agreed and starts out pending payment. A change order asks for money outside the contract: it starts out awaiting approval and is not billable until an admin confirms, in Accounts Receivable, that the client approved it.
sec.invoices-emitir.step.number.title: The system assigns the number
sec.invoices-emitir.step.number.body: One sequence per company and year: INV-2026-7 for invoices, COR-2026-3 for change orders. It does not come from the Invoice template. You can write your own; a repeat is rejected.
The jobsite rules, and tells you how much fits

Pick the jobsite and we tell you what is left to bill against its contract. Billing does not draw down the jobsite's budget: it is only compared against that ceiling, and going over it makes the server reject the document.
sec.invoices-emitir.step.line-items.titl: This is what the client will see
sec.invoices-emitir.step.line-items.body: Each line is quantity times price, and the subtotal works itself out. It is the breakdown printed on the PDF.
sec.invoices-emitir.step.totals.title: The total is what is left to collect
sec.invoices-emitir.step.totals.body: You type the discount and the tax rate. The result becomes a receivable — except on a change order, which collects nothing until it is approved.
sec.invoice-branding.step.logo.title: This logo goes on every PDF
sec.invoice-branding.step.logo.body: PNG or JPG up to 2 MB. It appears in the header of every invoice and change order, and in your team's app too. With none uploaded, your company's initials are used.
sec.invoice-branding.step.fields.title: These are your details, not the client's
sec.invoice-branding.step.fields.body: The issuer's, printed at the top of the invoice: name, contact, address, email and phone. The client's come from their record in Clients.
sec.invoice-branding.step.save.title: Nothing applies until you save
sec.invoice-branding.step.save.body: The logo included. The bar at the foot counts what is pending, and invoices already issued are never altered.
sec.budgets.step.header.title: The budget is not created here
sec.budgets.step.header.body: It is created with the project. This screen watches and adjusts it — the cost budget, the contract and the close — and every change stays in the history.
sec.budgets.step.kpis.title: Four figures, not one
sec.budgets.step.kpis.body: Contract is what you bill; cost budget is what you plan to spend. Spent adds three sources: approved expenses, supplier payments and payroll. Margin is contract minus spent.
sec.expense-report.step.export.title: Exports the aggregated report
sec.expense-report.step.export.body: By project and by worker — not the list of individual expenses.
sec.expense-report.step.filters.title: It does not refresh on its own
sec.expense-report.step.filters.body: Change the parameters and press "Generate report". The green "generated" tag confirms what you see matches those parameters.
sec.expense-report.step.kpis.title: "Total approved" leaves out the pending
sec.expense-report.step.kpis.body: It only counts expenses that already went through your approval in the Expenses screen. Pending and rejected ones are not in this figure.
sec.expense-report.step.by-project.title: Each job, with its breakdown
sec.expense-report.step.by-project.body: It splits how much is approved, pending, observed and rejected. The row expands to see the split by expense category.
sec.office-expenses.step.kpis.title: Careful with the second number
sec.office-expenses.step.kpis.body: It adds up only the expenses on the page you are looking at, not the whole history. The first one is the true total for the filter.
sec.office-expenses.step.new-expense.tit: These expenses belong to no job site
sec.office-expenses.step.new-expense.bod: Rent, software, stationery. That is why you record them by hand and they draw down no project's budget.
sec.office-expenses.step.filters.title: The dates are purchase dates
sec.office-expenses.step.filters.body: They filter by the purchase date you typed in the form, not by when you recorded the expense in the system.
sec.accounts-payable.step.new-bill.title: This is where you record what is billed TO you
sec.accounts-payable.step.new-bill.body: Material suppliers, machinery rental, subcontractors — each with its due date.
sec.accounts-payable.step.kpis.title: "Overdue" saves you surcharges
sec.accounts-payable.step.kpis.body: Supplier invoices whose payment term has passed. This is the list that keeps you from paying interest or losing supply.
sec.accounts-payable.step.filters.title: Assigning a bill to a job has a consequence
sec.accounts-payable.step.filters.body: The project filter reflects that assignment, and it is what makes the amount draw down that job's budget.
sec.accounts-payable.step.table.title: The "balance" column is what is left
sec.accounts-payable.step.table.body: What remains unpaid on each invoice. Click the row to see payments already made and the document images.
sec.users.step.new-user.title: Two ways to add your people
sec.users.step.new-user.body: "Invite by QR" generates a code the worker scans with their phone to enrol themselves. "New user" is the manual path, where you type in the name, role and hourly rate.
sec.users.step.kpis.title: Watch the middle number: "no PIN"
sec.users.step.kpis.body: It counts field users you have not issued a credential to yet. Without a PIN a worker cannot clock in on the site tablet. It is a button: tap it to filter the list down to just those.
sec.users.step.filters.title: The access filter splits two worlds
sec.users.step.filters.body: FIELD is the people who clock in on site; OFFICE is the people who log into this web panel. It comes from the role you picked when you created each user.
sec.users.step.roster.title: The roster is grouped by role
sec.users.step.roster.body: You will see FIELD and OFFICE blocks. An orange bar on the left of a row means that worker is missing their PIN; click the row and the panel where you generate it opens.
sec.time-approvals.step.kpis.title: "With alerts" is what to check first
sec.time-approvals.step.kpis.body: These are the entries the system flagged on its own: an over-long shift, no clock-out, or a jump between projects. The hours in the third indicator are the ones that have not reached payroll yet.
sec.time-approvals.step.filters.title: You land filtered to PENDING, this week
sec.time-approvals.step.filters.body: Switch the status to APPROVED or OBSERVED to review what you already decided — an approved entry leaves this inbox.
sec.time-approvals.step.queue.title: Each row is one worker's day
sec.time-approvals.step.queue.body: With its sequence of punches. The orange border marks the ones carrying an alert. The row's "approve" button turns those hours into approved hours, the only ones payroll pays.
sec.projects.step.kpis.title: Three numbers that ask for action
sec.projects.step.kpis.body: Active, incomplete and in the red. An incomplete jobsite takes no expenses or change orders until it has a client, a code and a contract.
sec.projects.step.filters.title: Filter and find the jobsite
sec.projects.step.filters.body: Search by name or combine status, client and incomplete record. The filters stay on while you work in this section.
sec.projects.step.table.title: The bar warns before it hurts
sec.projects.step.table.body: Spent against the budget, or the contract if there is none. Ink means fine, orange means past 90%, red means you spent more than you signed.
sec.projects.step.menu.title: CLOSED doesn't delete, it freezes
sec.projects.step.menu.body: Closing leaves the jobsite read-only and keeps its whole history. Deleting only works on clean jobsites, with no expenses, hours or invoices.
sec.projects-crear.step.identity.title: No client, no accounting
sec.projects-crear.step.identity.body: Client and cost code tie the jobsite to its invoices and expenses. Without them the record stays incomplete and accounting stays blocked.
sec.projects-crear.step.money.title: What you bill and what you spend
sec.projects-crear.step.money.body: The contract is what you bill the client. The cost budget is what you plan to spend; fill it in and progress is measured against it.
sec.projects-crear.step.address.title: Pick the address and you're done
sec.projects-crear.step.address.body: Type and tap a suggestion: the coordinates fill in by themselves. You can also drag the pin if the jobsite has no street number.
sec.projects-crear.step.geofence.title: The radius flags, it never blocks
sec.projects-crear.step.geofence.body: Anyone clocking in outside this radius is flagged for the supervisor to review. They are never stopped from clocking in.
sec.projects-ficha-resumen.step.bar.titl: Everything about the jobsite, up top
sec.projects-ficha-resumen.step.bar.body: The jobsite lives here: its status, its code and its client. These buttons assign the crew, edit the record or share the portal.
sec.projects-ficha-resumen.step.map.titl: Where it is and how far
sec.projects-ficha-resumen.step.map.body: The pin is the jobsite and the circle is the geofence. Open Edit to change them; here they are read-only.
sec.projects-ficha-resumen.step.team.bod: These are the users allowed to clock in at this jobsite. Tap See team to add or remove people.
sec.projects-ficha-dinero.step.billing.b: Invoiced is what you issued, collected what came in, owed is the difference, and spent is what already left your pocket.
The original is what you signed. The revised one adds and subtracts change orders: when they differ, the revised figure turns orange.
sec.projects-ficha-dinero.step.co-form.b: Every increase or deduction is saved as a change order with its amount and reason, and moves the revised contract instantly.
sec.projects-ficha-dinero.step.history.b: The full list of how the contract reached its current amount: what changed, when, by how much and the balance after.
sec.projects-ficha-equipo.step.table.bod: These are the workers who can clock in at this jobsite from the mobile app. Assign nobody and nobody can clock in here.
sec.projects-ficha-equipo.step.assign.ti: Add and remove in one step
sec.projects-ficha-equipo.step.assign.bo: Two lists open: available and assigned. Before saving it tells you how many are added and how many removed.
sec.projects-ficha-pendientes.step.state: The path of a punch item
From reported to in progress, then ready for review and finally closed. If the client does not approve it, it comes back as bounced.
sec.projects-ficha-pendientes.step.origi: The client's items show on their portal and they confirm them. Internal ones are yours alone: the client never sees them.
sec.projects-ficha-pendientes.step.ready: Marking ready attaches photos and a note. That is what the client sees to confirm it was resolved.
sec.projects-ficha-pendientes.step.revie: If the client does not answer
Seven days after ready for review you can close it yourself. Mind that the comment thread is visible to the client on their portal.
While it is a draft only your crew sees it. Sending it assigns a number, reaches the client and can no longer be deleted.
sec.projects-ficha-consultas.step.turn.b: Our move or the client's, depending on who must answer. Overdue means the deadline you set has passed.
sec.projects-ficha-consultas.step.impact: Note whether the answer moves cost or schedule. It stays on record and backs the change order.
sec.projects-ficha-consultas.step.offici: When closing you pick which reply in the thread is the official one. That is what stays on the project's record.
sec.projects-ficha-portal.step.link.titl: One link and they are in
sec.projects-ficha-portal.step.link.body: The client scans or opens the link and sees the site log, punch list and RFIs. Nothing to install, no account.
sec.projects-ficha-portal.step.pin.title: Add a PIN, it takes ten seconds
sec.projects-ficha-portal.step.pin.body: Anyone with the link can see the jobsite. With a six-digit PIN only those who have it get in; share it separately from the link.
sec.projects-ficha-portal.step.expiry.bo: Pick 30, 60, 90 or 180 days. Regenerating invalidates the previous link at once, and revoking cuts access instantly.
sec.expenses.step.approve-all.title: Approve in bulk
sec.expenses.step.approve-all.body: Approves every pending expense in the current filter at once; the bubble shows how many. Once approved they start drawing down their project's budget.
sec.expenses.step.kpis.title: "Observed" is not rejected
sec.expenses.step.kpis.body: It is an expense you sent back to the worker to fix the amount or re-upload the receipt. It can still be approved afterwards.
sec.expenses.step.filters.title: These filters do not apply themselves
sec.expenses.step.filters.body: Set dates, worker, project or type and press "Apply". Below it tells you how many expenses match and how many are still pending.
sec.expenses.step.table.title: The receipt column is the point
sec.expenses.step.table.body: It opens the photo of the receipt the worker took with their phone, zoomable. That is what you check before approving the amount.
sec.accounts-receivable.step.kpis.title: "Overdue" is money you should already have
sec.accounts-receivable.step.kpis.body: Invoices whose due date has passed and are still not fully paid. You set that date when you issued the invoice.
sec.accounts-receivable.step.filters.bod: These are invoices where the client paid part of it; the remaining balance still counts inside the pending total.
sec.accounts-receivable.step.table.title: Every row expands
sec.accounts-receivable.step.table.body: It shows the invoice line items and the history of payments received. That is where you record a new payment.
sec.audit.step.kpis.title: "Alerts" are failed attempts
sec.audit.step.kpis.body: Rejected logins or actions without permission. If that number climbs with no explanation, someone is trying to get in where they should not.
sec.audit.step.filters.title: The person filter fills itself
sec.audit.step.filters.body: Only with users who actually generated events in the chosen period, not your whole payroll.
sec.audit.step.list.title: This log cannot be touched
sec.audit.step.list.body: Each line is who did what and when. Not even you as an administrator can edit or delete it: it is written automatically and stands as evidence in a labour dispute or an audit.
sec.users.title: Users — your crew starts here
sec.users.body: Add workers, supervisors and office staff, and generate the QR badge they use to clock in from their phone.
sec.users.b1: Create the user, assign their role, hand them their QR badge.
sec.users.b2: Someone leaves? Deactivate them here and access ends instantly.
sec.time-approvals.title: Time Approvals — hours go through you
sec.time-approvals.body: Every shift your crew clocks lands here as pending. Nothing counts toward pay until you approve it.
sec.time-approvals.b1: Review each punch's in/out times and location.
sec.time-approvals.b2: Approve or correct same-day so payroll rolls out by itself.
sec.hours.title: Hours Report — how much each person worked
sec.hours.body: Approved hours by worker and jobsite, for any date range you pick.
sec.hours.b1: Filter by jobsite or person to answer "how many hours so far?".
sec.hours.b2: Export the report to back up payroll.
sec.labor-cost.title: Labor Cost — hours turned into money
sec.labor-cost.body: Crosses approved hours with each worker's rate so you know what labor costs per jobsite.
sec.labor-cost.b1: Spot which jobsite is eating the budget in labor.
sec.labor-cost.b2: Check it before quoting the next similar job.
sec.labor-payroll.title: Payroll — what's due, and what you already paid
sec.labor-payroll.body: Summarizes approved and unpaid hours per worker for the period you set, without ever letting you pay the same shift twice.
sec.labor-payroll.b1: Mark what you've paid — the trail stays.
sec.labor-payroll.b2: "Payments to Excel" downloads the cheques you ALREADY wrote in the period — one line per cheque, with the breakdown by job — ready to key into QuickBooks.
sec.projects.title: Projects — every jobsite lives here
sec.projects.body: Create your jobsites with contract, location and geofence. Almost everything else (hours, expenses, invoices) ties back to one.
sec.projects.b1: Set the geofence so off-site punches get flagged.
sec.projects.b2: Assign workers so the jobsite shows up in their app.
sec.projects-crear.title: Create jobsite — name and contract, the rest later
sec.projects-crear.body: Client and code tie down the accounting; the map and geofence say where clock-ins happen.
sec.projects-crear.b1: The cost budget is optional: fill it in and progress is measured against it.
sec.projects-crear.b2: The geofence radius flags far-away clock-ins for review; it never blocks them.
sec.projects-ficha-resumen.title: Summary — the whole jobsite on one card
sec.projects-ficha-resumen.body: What was signed, where it is and who works it, in one view.
sec.projects-ficha-resumen.b1: The map is read-only: open Edit to move it.
sec.projects-ficha-resumen.b2: The assigned users are the ones who can clock in here; tap See team to change them.
sec.projects-ficha-dinero.title: Money — contract, collections and change orders
sec.projects-ficha-dinero.body: Invoiced, collected, what you are owed and what was spent, plus the contract and its history.
sec.projects-ficha-dinero.b1: Every change order moves the revised contract instantly.
sec.projects-ficha-dinero.b2: The balance is the budget base minus what was spent.
sec.projects-ficha-equipo.title: Team — who can clock in at this jobsite
sec.projects-ficha-equipo.body: Assigned users see the jobsite in their app and can clock in.
sec.projects-ficha-equipo.b1: Assign nobody and nobody clocks in here.
sec.projects-ficha-equipo.b2: Assign users opens two lists: available and assigned.
sec.projects-ficha-pendientes.title: Punch list — the fixes still owed
sec.projects-ficha-pendientes.body: From the client or from your crew, with evidence photos and a comment thread.
sec.projects-ficha-pendientes.b1: Marking ready attaches photos and a note the client sees to confirm.
sec.projects-ficha-pendientes.b2: If the client does not answer within seven days, you can close it yourself.
sec.projects-ficha-consultas.title: RFIs — formal questions to the client
sec.projects-ficha-consultas.body: Every RFI carries a number, a deadline and cost and schedule impacts.
sec.projects-ficha-consultas.b1: A draft is seen only by your crew; sending it reaches the client.
sec.projects-ficha-consultas.b2: When closing you pick which reply in the thread is the official one.
sec.projects-ficha-portal.title: Portal — the client's link
sec.projects-ficha-portal.body: A read-only link the client uses to follow the jobsite without installing anything.
sec.projects-ficha-portal.b1: Protect it with a six-digit PIN and share that separately from the link.
sec.projects-ficha-portal.b2: Regenerating invalidates the previous link; revoking cuts access instantly.
sec.clients.title: Clients — who hires you
sec.clients.body: Your client directory and its link to each jobsite, including client-portal access.
sec.clients.b1: Tie each jobsite to its client to keep billing tidy.
sec.clients.b2: Share the portal so they see progress without calling you.
sec.clients-ficha.title: Client record — who to call and what you build for them
sec.clients-ficha.body: Its contact and billing details, and all its jobsites in one view.
sec.clients-ficha.b1: Copy its billing details without retyping them.
sec.clients-ficha.b2: Create a jobsite from here and it opens with the client already picked.
sec.subcontractors.title: Subcontractors — third-party work under control
sec.subcontractors.body: Who you work with, what you assigned them and what they bill you: the section's three tabs.
sec.subcontractors.b1: Document what you received with photos; no more "but I finished it".
sec.subcontractors.b2: Keep each subcontract's balance in sight.
sec.subcontractors-jobs.title: Jobs — what you assign
sec.subcontractors-jobs.body: Every job with its agreed amount, its due date and what the subcontractor has uploaded.
sec.subcontractors-jobs.b1: "In review" is the queue waiting on your sign-off.
sec.subcontractors-jobs.b2: The search looks at every page, not just the one you see.
sec.subcontractors-ficha.title: Job detail — the proof and the decision
sec.subcontractors-ficha.body: Approve or send back, with the evidence and the conversation in front of you.
sec.subcontractors-ficha.b1: The money strip says how much you owe on this job.
sec.subcontractors-ficha.b2: The history can't be edited or deleted: it is your record.
sec.schedules.title: Tasks — the day's report
sec.schedules.body: Every task across your projects in one list, ordered by what's due first.
sec.schedules.b1: Assign, advance a step and close them without leaving the row.
sec.schedules.b2: Read it on Monday morning: overdue first, then what's due today.
sec.schedules-semana.title: The week — who is overloaded
sec.schedules-semana.body: The same tasks with time on the axis: rows of people or projects, columns of days.
sec.schedules-semana.b1: A bar that runs past the week says so with its edge mark and its date.
sec.schedules-semana.b2: Tasks with no dates live in the drawer below, always in sight.
sec.tool-inventory.title: Tools — what you own and who has it
sec.tool-inventory.body: Two inventories in one screen: what's lent and returned, and what's used up and restocked. Here you register, fix and look things up.
sec.tool-inventory.b1: Register a tool with its code and fix its status when you need to.
sec.tool-inventory.b2: Assigning, returning and dispatching happen in the warehouse, with the person there.
sec.tool-report.title: Tool report — what you have, what hasn't come back and what's being used up
sec.tool-report.body: Four questions in one screen: what you have and in what state, what hasn't come back, who has what and what's being used up.
sec.tool-report.b1: See the breakdown by status and by category, with percentages computed over what you are seeing.
sec.tool-report.b2: Spot the tools that never came back: what's been out too long and what left with nobody signing.
sec.invoices.title: Invoices — what you issue
sec.invoices.body: Everything you have billed your clients, and the window that issues an invoice or a change order.
sec.invoices.b1: Your company's details come from the Invoice template. The numbering is assigned by the system: one sequence per company and year.
sec.invoices.b2: The PDF uses your logo and the details on your letterhead, in the panel's language. The document's colours are not configurable.
sec.invoice-branding.title: Invoice Template — your identity on paper
sec.invoice-branding.body: Name, logo and contact details shown on every invoice PDF. It also feeds the mobile app's logo.
sec.invoice-branding.b1: Upload your logo once and every invoice carries it.
sec.invoice-branding.b2: The same name and logo identify your company in the crew app.
sec.budgets.title: Budgets — what each project costs against what it bills
sec.budgets.body: Every project's contract, its cost budget, what has been spent and the margin. And in the second view, what you are owed and where the money went.
sec.budgets.b1: Change orders are recorded on the project's own page. Here they show added into the contract.
sec.budgets.b2: The Projects | Report switcher changes the body; the filter you set holds for both.
sec.expenses.title: Expenses — what the crew spends in the field
sec.expenses.body: Expenses your people log (fuel, materials, freight) land here for your approval, receipt photo included.
sec.expenses.b1: Approve or observe each one; only approved spend burns budget.
sec.expenses.b2: The dashboard reminds you of the pending amount.
sec.expense-report.title: Expense Report — where the money goes
sec.expense-report.body: Expense totals by jobsite, type and period, with export.
sec.expense-report.b1: Find the category that spiked this month.
sec.expense-report.b2: Back up settlements with the exported detail.
sec.office-expenses.title: Office Expenses — what isn't jobsite cost
sec.office-expenses.body: Rent, utilities, supplies: administrative spend kept separate from jobsite costs.
sec.office-expenses.b2: Log recurring ones so they never surprise you.
sec.accounts-receivable.title: Accounts Receivable — get paid
sec.accounts-receivable.body: Invoices and change orders issued to clients: what's pending, what's overdue, and partial collections.
sec.accounts-receivable.b1: Record every collection (even partial) and the balance updates.
sec.accounts-receivable.b2: Overdue shows orange on the dashboard — chase it from here.
sec.accounts-payable.title: Accounts Payable — who you owe
sec.accounts-payable.body: Your vendors' bills with due dates, so you pay on time without surprises.
sec.accounts-payable.b1: Log the bill when it arrives and the due date warns you.
sec.accounts-payable.b2: The next 7 days show on the dashboard.
sec.audit.title: Audit Log — everything on record
sec.audit.body: Every important action in the system: who did what, when, and from where. Your backup whenever questions come up.
sec.audit.b1: Filter by person or action to reconstruct what happened.
sec.audit.b2: No one can erase history — not even the admin.
sec.tm-field.title: Time & material — unplanned work, signed on site
sec.tm-field.body: On a remodel, work shows up that was never in the contract. The formal change order takes days; this is the usual paper routine, made system: agree it on site, do it, and the client's superintendent signs. That signature is what later becomes a change order.
sec.tm-field.b1: Capture the ticket as soon as the work is finished, dated the day it was done.
sec.tm-field.b2: Ask for the signature on the spot: on this same device, or by sending the link.
sec.tm-office.title: Time & material — from signature to change order
sec.tm-office.body: What the site already did and the client already signed lands here. The signature moves no money: converting does — it raises the contract and writes the entry in its history, and it cannot be undone. That step is decided at this desk.
sec.tm-office.b1: Watch the age: a signed ticket growing old is money not being billed.
sec.tm-office.b2: Only a signed ticket gets converted. A declined one goes back to the site to be fixed.
sec.tm-field.step.pending.title: Work done that nobody has authorized yet
sec.tm-field.step.pending.body: Money for work already executed that is still waiting on a signature or on the office, and how many days the oldest has been waiting. This number is on no other screen.
sec.tm-field.step.new.title: Capture the work as soon as it is done
sec.tm-field.step.new.body: People, hours, rate and material — the total works itself out as you type. And mind the date: it is the day the work was done, not today. Tuesday's entry is usually Monday's work.
sec.tm-field.step.list.title: Asking for the signature freezes the ticket
sec.tm-field.step.list.body: Click a ticket to open it. When it is ready, "Get it signed" freezes it: it can no longer be edited, because what the client signs has to be exactly what was saved.
sec.tm-field.step.sign.title: The client's superintendent is the one who signs
sec.tm-field.step.sign.body: They can sign right here — you hand over the phone and the screen stays locked on the document — or you copy the link and send it to them. While you wait for the signature, you can withdraw the request.
sec.tm-field.step.states.title: "Did not sign" is not "has not signed yet"
sec.tm-field.step.states.body: Both are unauthorized work, but only one is still waiting. A declined ticket becomes editable again: fix it and ask for the signature again. A signed one waits for the office to convert it.
sec.tm-office.step.pending.title: What is waiting on this desk
sec.tm-office.step.pending.body: Work already executed that is still waiting on a signature or on this desk, with the age of the oldest. When those days grow, something is falling asleep.
sec.tm-office.step.queue.title: Only what is signed gets converted
sec.tm-office.step.queue.body: A signature converts nothing by itself: it leaves the ticket ready, and someone here decides. Open a signed ticket and the button is there; an unsigned one does not offer it.
sec.tm-office.step.convert.title: Converting is the step that moves money
sec.tm-office.step.convert.body: It raises the job's contract amount and writes the entry in its history. It cannot be undone from any screen — which is why it asks you to confirm first.
